parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a restrictive parent framework on a division with documented hostility. Traveller-facing exposures: entry document regime (X markers barred, mismatch triggers refusal and possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings, foreign travel advisories); documented birth-sex custody placement (men's ward after bathroom arrest; male-guard search in men's jail despite female licence marker) with no shown remedy; federal corrections conversion-therapy policy and immigrationcustody abuse; a 2026 mob beating where victims were charged, attackers unarrested, and one denied hospital care; no state gender-identity discrimination law, lowest equality band; severe municipal restroom ordinance. Mitigations: national hate-crime statute, active litigation and legal-aid resources, two municipalities with public-accommodation protections. No statewide facilities ban is established. Net: unremedied state-imposed exposures plus failed recourse — below 0.35 anchors' single-exposure profile on balance but above police-raid/organised-extortion tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order/foreign-ministry rule ends X and non-assigned-sex markers; Supreme Court allowed it Nov 2025. Officers told to refuse where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and consider fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Trans travellers report confiscated/blocked passports and strandings; eight-plus governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid to expiration; new issues processed as M/F per supporting documents; ACLU-style suit pending; legal-aid FAQ guides document strategy.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry doubt can escalate from refusal to fraud finding affecting all future travel; feeds visa case-note tagging for trans applicants.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Birth-sex placement documented twice: trans student held 24h in men's ward after bathroom arrest (Mar 2025); Aug 2026 mob victim jailed in men's facility and searched by male guard despite female licence marker. Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; passport and order challenges pending. No documented remedy for custody placement.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facilities arrest routes directly into birth-sex custody and male search; immigration custody is reachable by a visitor through entry disputes.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Municipality passed one of the country's most severe anti-trans restroom ordinances (Aug 2026). Parent map: bans in 22+ state/provinces across categories, 4 making use criminal in some circumstances, 6 extending to private settings; a Feb 2026 state law elsewhere invalidates non-matching documents and bars sex-segregated facility use as a 'template'.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Statewide facilities statute for this division not established; trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility confrontation is the documented trigger for both the arrest and the mob attack, each flowing into custody and criminal charges against the trans person.

care_services.exposure: Aug 2026 mob victim denied hospital care before being taken to jail. State banned gender-affirming care for minors effective 1 Jan 2024 — operative for a travelling family with a trans minor. Federal proposal would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: Emergency-care access generally not restricted by national policy; some orders enjoined. No documented visitor care-assurance mechanism.
care_services.interaction: Care seeking after an incident can out the traveller and, for minors, meets an operative ban; denied care here followed directly from custody processing.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among viewpoints animating violent extremists; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups 'radically pro-transgender'; January 2025 order calls minors' care 'mutilation'; advocates compare the record to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo states ideology is never the reward criterion; strategy says powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing shapes how patrol officers and prosecutors treat the trans person in the documented incidents where victims, not attackers, were charged.

minors_guardians.exposure: EO directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; state care ban for minors since 2024; school-sports bar; federal record subpoenas for under-19s. A trans minor's passport falls under the same marker regime.
minors_guardians.protection: Litigation pending on several orders; no documented traveller-facing shield for families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting parent with a trans minor faces document refusal at entry plus unavailable affirming care at destination; a cis-minor family is largely unaffected beyond entry checks.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 mob beat a trans couple over restroom use; both victims charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker arrested, one denied care. State response is damning: charging victims and inaction. Trans inmate killed in prison fight (2024). State hate-crime law excludes gender identity. The 24.7/100k killing figure is an undercount floor and near the comparison state's — unusable as rate evidence.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, so federal prosecution is available; national media and rights groups documented the attack.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State statute's gap pushes recourse to federal prosecutors whose response to this incident is not recorded; absence of attacker arrests signals impunity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcome of passport suit, EO challenges and plea deal unresolved; whether officers actually impose fraud findings unknown; statewide facilities position not established; killing-rate true value unknowable as an undercount floor; custody placement beyond the two documented cases unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple pending suits, legal-aid FAQ, national equality/identity-document trackers, and two municipalities barring gender-identity discrimination including public accommodations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation means exposure varies by moment of travel; partial municipal protections reach visitors only within those two municipalities.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a birth-sex public-building rule upheld by courts with rejected complaints and no offence of being trans. This dossier shares the unremedied state-imposed tier (custody birth-sex placement with male search, severe municipal ordinance, no state discrimination law) but adds a parent entry-document regime with refusal/fraud exposure and a recent mob beating where victims were charged — more exposures than 0.35-A, so it rates slightly below.

0.45-B features a custody birth-sex rule with repeated humiliation, ineffective oversight, but prosecutions of assaults and mostly normal service elsewhere. This case has the same custody exposure plus documented care denial, victims-charged/no-attacker-arrest response, and entry-document refusal risk — worse state response and an extra universal layer, so materially below 0.45.

0.55-B has hostile ferry/guesthouse treatment with mediators securing refunds, an assault conviction, and no compulsory placement rule. Here the exposures are state-imposed (custody placement, entry documents, care denial) with no demonstrated remedy and a impunity-flavoured violence response — a full tier lower than 0.55.

0.75-C pairs acceptance, accepted foreign documents, enforced compensation for lodging refusal and only an open question on custody. This dossier inverts each: refused/mismatched documents, documented birth-sex custody abuse, failed violence response, no state protections. Far below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The parent framework supplies continuous traveller-facing exposure: entry officers are instructed to doubt sex from documents, may refuse cases and consider lifetime fraud findings, X markers are gone, and foreign governments now warn their trans citizens away. Within that, the division adds documented consequences of discovery — birth-sex custody with male-guard search despite a matching licence, a mob beating where the trans victims were charged and no attacker arrested, one victim denied hospital care, a severe municipal restroom ordinance, and no state gender-identity discrimination law. Recourse exists only at national level (hate-crime statute, pending suits, two protective municipalities) and is unshown operating here. Paper protections plus active civil society cushion the floor, but the operative pattern is state-imposed exposure with failed remedy, placing this in the lower Elevated Risk band.
